# Agentic ODI [![Open the Living Studio](https://img.shields.io/badge/Open%20the%20Living%20Studio-F38020?style=for-the-badge&logo=cloudflare&logoColor=white)](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/) [![CI](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/actions/workflows/ci.yml) [![codecov](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi/branch/main/graph/badge.svg)](https://codecov.io/gh/alehar9320/agentic-odi) [![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.10%2B-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/downloads/) [![uv](https://img.shields.io/badge/uv-managed-green)](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) [![Ruff](https://img.shields.io/endpoint?url=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/astral-sh/ruff/main/assets/badge/v2.json)](https://github.com/astral-sh/ruff) [![FastMCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/FastMCP-powered-orange)](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp) [![pytest](https://img.shields.io/badge/tests-pytest-blue)](https://pytest.org) [![MCP](https://img.shields.io/badge/Model%20Context%20Protocol-enabled-8A2BE2)](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) > **[![Experimental](https://img.shields.io/badge/Experimental-1e293b?style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi)** > **Experimental test to learn and evaluate the feasibility of utilizing Model Context Protocol (MCP) for Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) specifications.**
--- > **See it live:** **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. > No install required; the interface loads immediately, while live data, chat, and > mutations need the local sidecar ([Deployment](docs/deployment.md)). To run the > full stack yourself, jump to [Quick Start](#quick-start). **Agentic ODI** explores how the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) can turn [Outcome-Driven Innovation](https://strategyn.com/outcome-driven-innovation/) into a live, agent-queryable source of context. Instead of feeding LLMs disconnected prompts, an MCP-powered ODI server acts as the "brain" of customer needs — letting agents invent, evaluate, and ideate solutions anchored in verified, measurable customer outcomes (Job Maps, Desired Outcomes, and Opportunity Scores). This repository is an experimental testbed for understanding server–client MCP communication streams, built on [`FastMCP`](https://github.com/jlowin/fastmcp). We don't publish dates. This page changes when the code does. **Project site:** the site lives at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/)**, with a documentation hub at **[alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/)**. It is republished by the `Pages` workflow on every push to `main`. The site is generated from this repository — the MCP tool reference, the connector catalog, the CLI tree, and the ODI schema are read from the code that ships, so they cannot drift from it. **Hosted Studio:** the experimental Living Studio UI runs at **[agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev](https://agentic-odi.alehar.workers.dev/)**. It loads without a backend; live data needs the sidecar tunnel described in [Deployment](docs/deployment.md). Pull requests get preview URLs from Cloudflare Workers Builds. ## Code Overview A [uv workspace](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/concepts/projects/workspaces/) with shared tooling at the root. Packages live in `packages/`, runnable services in `apps/`, and deployment assets in `infra/`: | Path | Distribution | Description | |---|---|---| | **`packages/core/`** | `agentic-odi-core` | Domain models, the `ODIService` business-logic layer, repository implementations (in-memory and SQLite), the shared MCP tool contract, and ODI opportunity-score computation. | | **`packages/connectors/`** | `agentic-odi-connectors` | Pluggable MCP and REST connectors with presets and an ingest sink. | | **`apps/mcp-server/`** | `agentic-odi-mcp-server` | FastMCP server exposing Jobs, Steps, Desired Outcomes, Customer Outcomes, Evidence, and context tools over HTTP. Persists to SQLite by default. | | **`apps/studio-api/`** | `agentic-odi-studio-api` | FastAPI **Living Studio sidecar**. Serves config, health, canvas data, local mutations, MCP passthrough, SSE chat, conversation history, and the PM memory store, plus the built SPA. | | **`apps/cli/`** | `agentic-odi-cli` | Typer CLI with interactive chat plus full entity CRUD, `schema`, `connectors`, and local-first (`--backend local`) or remote (`--backend mcp`) data access. | | **`apps/studio/`** | React + TypeScript + Vite | **The Living Studio** SPA and Tauri 2 desktop shell. The copilot renders **agent-composed surfaces inline** — scored outcomes, opportunity theses, bet simulations — from a closed catalog the SPA owns. A feature-flagged **four-step first-run tour** starts from the PM's ambition, and a local memory records what matters across sessions. | | **`infra/cloudflare/`** | Worker | Free-plan Workers Static Assets deployment and sidecar tunnel. | | **`scripts/`** | — | Dev launcher, binary build, installer tests. | | **`tests/contract/`** | — | Cross-package MCP contract tests. | See [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) for the dependency graph, data flow, and testing strategy. ## Quick Start **Prerequisites:** Python 3.10+ and the [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/) package manager. ```bash # Install the entire workspace (all five Python projects plus dev tooling) uv sync --all-packages # Build the Studio SPA, then launch the MCP server and Living Studio together npm --prefix apps/studio run build python scripts/dev.py ``` | Service | URL | |---|---| | MCP Server | http://localhost:8000/mcp | | The Living Studio | http://127.0.0.1:8100 | For hot reload, `npm --prefix apps/studio run dev:full` starts the MCP server, the sidecar, and Vite together on http://localhost:5173. For the desktop app, use `npm --prefix apps/studio run tauri dev`. See [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md). The first time you open the Studio, the tour asks what you want to win: an opportunity you already have in mind, a priority your boss handed you, finding the next opportunity, or pressure-testing a bet. Pick one and the conversation starts there — no form, no framework speech. It still asks for your product and audience when it needs them, and everything you say is optional and skippable. After that it opens as one room: the transcript and the composer never leave the screen. Describe a job or a customer frustration, or type `/` for commands that mirror the CLI. Whatever the thread produces — scored outcomes, an opportunity thesis, a job map, customer evidence — arrives as an inline surface, and a quiet rail above the conversation opens it in a lens that docks beside the thread instead of replacing it. Capture and simulation are conversations too: tell the studio what a customer said, or what bet you are weighing, and it renders the card. Use the bell to **catch up on outcome shifts, simulations, and telemetry signals while you were away**. The studio also remembers the person, not just the canvas. As you talk it notes what matters — your role, the opportunity, business constraints, stakeholders, evidence, how you like to work — and shows each note under **What I know** so you can confirm, correct, add, or forget it. The thread and those notes resume on the next launch. Memory lives in `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db` (override with `AGENTIC_ODI_STUDIO_DB`, or use `:memory:` for tests) and never blocks a reply if it fails. **Forget everything** clears the notes and the thread. The Studio is better with an OpenAI-compatible LLM with tool-calling support (see the [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md)), but it does not depend on one: with no model reachable it says so and every job, step, and outcome remains editable by hand. ### Connectors (MCP ↔ Living Studio) Register MCP or REST connectors that the copilot can discover and invoke. - **Where they live**: a shared `connectors.json` registry. Override its location with `AGENTIC_ODI_CONNECTORS_CONFIG`; by default it is `~/.config/agentic-odi/connectors.json`. See [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md). - **In the Living Studio**: open the **Settings** drawer → **Connectors** to list, remove, or add one of the recommended presets (Notion, PostHog, Exa, Linear, GitHub). - **Conversationally**: tell the copilot "use Notion" / "add the GitHub connector". It emits an `add_connector` local tool (handled in-process) that writes the preset to the registry, plus a `connector` SSE event the Studio surfaces as a suggestion chip. Dismissing or accepting the chip also refreshes the list. - **API**: `GET/POST/DELETE /api/connectors`, `GET /api/connectors/catalog`, and `GET /api/connectors/{name}/health` (the catalog honors `?area=` and `?recommended=true`). - **CLI**: `agentic-odi connectors catalog | add | list | health | ingest `. ### CLI at a glance The CLI is local-first, so data commands work without a running server: ```bash python -m agentic_odi_cli --version # print the Agentic ODI version python -m agentic_odi_cli --help # show available options and commands python -m agentic_odi_cli # start interactive chat in a terminal agentic-odi jobs list # Jobs-to-be-Done agentic-odi steps list --job-id agentic-odi desired-outcomes list --job-id agentic-odi customer-outcomes list agentic-odi evidence list --job-id agentic-odi schema # canonical JSON schema for every entity agentic-odi framework-guidelines # ODI stage-by-stage tool guide agentic-odi capabilities # what the assistant can help with agentic-odi score 8 2 # ODI opportunity score → 14.00 ``` Add `--backend mcp` to route data commands through a running MCP server (`python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server`). See the [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md). ### Install the binary Prebuilt binaries are available for Linux, macOS, and Windows: ```bash curl -fsSL https://github.com/alehar9320/agentic-odi/releases/latest/download/install.sh | sh ``` The installer symlinks `odi`, `odipm`, `odi-cli`, and `agentic-odi` into `~/.local/bin/`. See [Installation](docs/installation.md) for the install layout, updates, and release automation. ## Documentation | Guide | Contents | |---|---| | [CLI Reference](docs/cli.md) | Backends, interactive chat, Jobs/Steps/desired Outcomes/Customer Outcomes/evidence, `connectors`, scoring, environment variables | | [External Connectors](docs/connectors.md) | The MCP ingest connector, presets, and the `Connector` protocol | | [Running The Living Studio](docs/living-studio.md) | First-run tour and its flag, local memory and conversation resume, interface, rich inline responses and the UI catalog, run modes, desktop signing and updates, agent-driven testing (`/dev`, `/test`) | | [Local LLM Backend](docs/local-llm.md) | Running a local OpenAI-compatible model with tool calling | | [Development](docs/development.md) | Lint, format, type checks, frontend checks, tests and the coverage map | | [Architecture](docs/architecture/README.md) | Workspace layout, dependency direction, data flow, and testing | | [Installation](docs/installation.md) | Binary install, updater behavior, and release automation | | [Deployment](docs/deployment.md) | Project site on GitHub Pages, Hosted Studio and PR preview URLs, the MCP server endpoint, and the free-plan Cloudflare Worker | | [Roadmap](docs/roadmap.md) | Completed and upcoming milestones | | [Superpowers](docs/superpowers.md) | Pi, OpenCode, and Freebuff integration | Every guide above is also published on the [project site](https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/docs/), rendered from these files. The site adds a quick start, a generated MCP tool reference, and the connector catalog. ## Contributing Contributions are welcome! This project uses [Ruff](https://docs.astral.sh/ruff/) for linting and formatting and [pytest](https://pytest.org/) for tests. Make sure your change passes the [lint, format, and test checks](docs/development.md) before opening a pull request. ## 🦦 Brand Odi the Otter is the mascot of Agentic ODI — a golden-ratio-derived pixel otter who appears in the CLI, the Living Studio, the desktop app icon, the favicon, and this page. The artwork is original, generated by a committed script, and documented in [brand/README.md](brand/README.md). ```bash uv run python brand/tools/render.py # regenerate every Odi asset ``` ## License This project is licensed under the terms of the MIT License — see [LICENSE](LICENSE) for details. ---
*Let's build AI that builds what people actually need.*

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

concurrency:
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

permissions:
  contents: read

  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Ruff Lint (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff check .

      - name: Verify Ruff Formatting (no auto-fix)
        run: uv run ruff format --check .

      - name: Verify the mascot assets match the generator
        run: uv run python brand/tools/render.py --check

  typecheck:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Mypy
        run: uv run mypy apps brand packages

      - name: Run Mypy (website)
        run: uv run --directory website mypy .

  security:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 10
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: Run Bandit
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages

      - name: Run Bandit (website)
        run: uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r website/

  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 20
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        python-version: ["3.10", "3.11", "3.12"]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: ${{ matrix.python-version }}

      - name: Pytest
        run: |
          uv run pytest \
            --cov=agentic_odi_cli \
            --cov=agentic_odi_connectors \
            --cov=agentic_odi_core \
            --cov=agentic_odi_mcp_server \
            --cov=agentic_odi_studio_api \
            --cov-report=term-missing \
            --cov-report=xml:coverage.xml

      - name: Upload coverage report
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: coverage-${{ matrix.python-version }}
          path: coverage.xml
          if-no-files-found: error

      # One upload per run is enough; the 3.12 report is the canonical one.
      - name: Upload coverage to Codecov
        if: ${{ matrix.python-version == '3.12' }}
        uses: codecov/codecov-action@v7
        with:
          token: ${{ secrets.CODECOV_TOKEN }}
          files: coverage.xml
          fail_ci_if_error: false

  smoke:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test]
    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      - name: CLI reports a version
        run: |
          version="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli --version)"
          [ -n "$version" ]
          echo "OK: $version"

      - name: CLI exposes connectors commands
        run: |
          help="$(uv run python -m agentic_odi_cli connectors --help)"
          echo "$help" | grep -q list
          echo "$help" | grep -q ingest
          echo "OK: connectors help"

      - name: Installer installs from a simulated release
        run: bash scripts/tests/install_e2e.sh

      - name: MCP server boots and serves /mcp
        run: |
          uv run python -m agentic_odi_mcp_server > /tmp/mcp_server.log 2>&1 &
          SERVER_PID=$!
          probe() {
            curl -sfX POST http://localhost:8000/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
              -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SERVER_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "MCP server did not respond on :8000/mcp"
            cat /tmp/mcp_server.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: MCP server responded with 200"

      - name: Living Studio sidecar serves the studio API

          AGENTIC_ODI_BACKEND=mcp uv run python -m agentic_odi_studio_api.main > /tmp/sidecar.log 2>&1 &

            curl -fsS -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/health/mcp \
              -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
              -d '{"mcp_url":"http://127.0.0.1:8000/mcp"}' -o /dev/null &&

          for _ in $(seq 1 30); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          kill "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          wait "$SIDECAR_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "Living Studio sidecar did not respond on :8100"
            cat /tmp/sidecar.log
            exit 1
          fi
          echo "OK: sidecar studio API responded with 200"

          uv run python scripts/dev.py > /tmp/clientrun.log 2>&1 &

          probe() {
            curl -sf -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:8100/api/config &&

                -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
                -d '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"initialize","id":1,"params":{"protocolVersion":"2024-11-05","capabilities":{},"clientInfo":{"name":"ci","version":"1"}}}' \
                -o /dev/null
          }
          ok=0
          for _ in $(seq 1 60); do
            if probe; then ok=1; break; fi
            sleep 1
          done
          if [ "$ok" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "scripts/dev.py did not bring up both services"
            cat /tmp/clientrun.log
            kill "$RUN_PID" 2>/dev/null || true
            exit 1
          fi
          kill -INT "$RUN_PID"
          wait "$RUN_PID"
          echo "OK: both services stopped cleanly"

    timeout-minutes: 15
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: ./.github/actions/setup

      # The site is generated and committed so a reviewer can read the
      # rendered HTML in a pull request. If the committed copy no longer
      # matches a fresh build, the site has drifted and the PR is not ready.
      - name: Check the committed site matches a fresh build

      - name: Pytest (website)

      - name: Build site
        run: uv run python website/tools/build_site.py --out _site

  studio:

    timeout-minutes: 15
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - name: Install dependencies
        run: npm ci

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Unit tests
        run: npm test -- --run

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      - name: Verify generated API types are up to date
        run: |
          npm run gen:api-types
          git diff --exit-code -- src/api/schema.d.ts

  tauri-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    defaults:
      run:
        shell: bash
        working-directory: apps/studio/src-tauri
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
        with:
          components: rustfmt, clippy

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Cargo fmt
        run: cargo fmt --check

      - name: Cargo clippy
        run: cargo clippy -- -D warnings

      - name: Cargo check
        run: cargo check

  tauri-build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 60
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7

      - name: Install Linux webview dependencies
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev build-essential curl wget file \
            libxdo-dev libssl-dev libayatana-appindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev patchelf

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: "lts/*"
          cache: npm
          cache-dependency-path: apps/studio/package-lock.json

      - uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable

      - uses: swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          workspaces: apps/studio/src-tauri -> target

      - name: Install frontend dependencies
        run: npm ci
        working-directory: apps/studio

      # Dependabot PRs cannot read repository secrets, so the signing key is
      # empty there. Export it only when present and disable updater artifacts
      # otherwise; passing an empty key makes the bundler try (and fail) to
      # decode it.
      - name: Build desktop bundle
        working-directory: apps/studio
        env:
          SIGNING_KEY: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY }}
          SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD: ${{ secrets.TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD }}
        run: |
          if [ -n "$SIGNING_KEY" ]; then
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY="$SIGNING_KEY"
            export TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY_PASSWORD="$SIGNING_KEY_PASSWORD"
            npm run tauri -- build
          else
            echo "No TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY provided — building without signed updater artifacts."
            npm run tauri -- build --config '{"bundle":{"createUpdaterArtifacts":false}}'
          fi

      - name: Upload desktop bundles
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: tauri-bundles-linux
          if-no-files-found: warn
          path: |
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/deb/*.deb
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage
            apps/studio/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/appimage/*.AppImage.sig

  ci-green:
    name: CI green
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    needs: [lint, typecheck, security, test, smoke, website, studio, tauri-check, tauri-build]
    if: always()
    steps:
      - name: Verify all required jobs succeeded
        run: |
          results='${{ join(needs.*.result, ' ') }}'
          echo "Job results: $results"
          for result in $results; do
            if [ "$result" != "success" ]; then
              echo "::error::A required job did not succeed ($results)"
              exit 1
            fi
          done
          echo "OK: all required jobs succeeded"

name: release

on:

jobs:
  build:
    strategy:
      fail-fast: false
      matrix:
        include:
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-latest
            target: linux_x86_64
          - os: linux
            runner: ubuntu-24.04-arm
            target: linux_arm64
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-14
            target: macos_arm64
          - os: macos
            runner: macos-15-intel
            target: macos_x86_64
          - os: windows
            runner: windows-latest
            target: windows_x86_64
    # No container: the Node-based actions (checkout, setup-uv) need glibc >= 2.28,
    # which the manylinux2014 images (glibc 2.17) cannot provide. If a narrower
    # glibc floor is needed later, use a manylinux_2_28 image instead.
    runs-on: ${{ matrix.runner }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup uv
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Build
        env:
          TARGET: ${{ matrix.target }}
        run: |
          VERSION="${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}"
          RELEASE_DATE_UTC="$(git log -1 --format=%cI)"
          export VERSION RELEASE_DATE_UTC
          bash scripts/build_binary.sh
      - name: Write checksums
        shell: bash
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          shopt -s nullglob
          archives=(odi_*.tar.gz odi_*.zip)
          if [ "${#archives[@]}" -eq 0 ]; then
            echo "::error::No archive was produced for ${{ matrix.target }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          if command -v sha256sum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            sha256sum "${archives[@]}" > "checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt"
          elif command -v shasum >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            shasum -a 256 "${archives[@]}" > "checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt"
          else
            echo "::error::No sha256 tool available on ${{ matrix.runner }}"
            exit 1
          fi
          cat "checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt"
      - name: Upload checksums fragment
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: checksums-${{ matrix.target }}
          path: checksums-${{ matrix.target }}.txt
          if-no-files-found: error
      - name: Upload assets
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            odi_*.tar.gz
            odi_*.zip

  checksums:
    needs: build
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/download-artifact@v8
        with:
          pattern: checksums-*
          path: fragments
          merge-multiple: true
      - name: Combine per-target checksums
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          cat fragments/checksums-*.txt | sort -k2 > checksums.txt
          test -s checksums.txt
          echo "checksums.txt"
          cat checksums.txt
      - name: Upload checksums.txt
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: checksums.txt

  upload-installers:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Upload install scripts
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v3
        with:
          files: |
            scripts/install.sh
            scripts/install.ps1

  release-instructions:
    needs: [checksums, upload-installers]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - name: Setup uv
        uses: ./.github/actions/setup
        with:
          python-version: "3.11"
      - name: Publish download & run instructions on the release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
        run: |
          python scripts/release_instructions.py \
            --tag "${{ github.ref_name }}" \
            --repo "${{ github.repository }}"

def _workflow() -> str:
    assert WORKFLOW.is_file(), (
        "missing .github/workflows/pages.yml: GitHub Pages deploys from a workflow, "
        "so without it https://alehar9320.github.io/agentic-odi/ 404s"
    )
    return WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def _ci_workflow() -> str:
    assert CI_WORKFLOW.is_file(), "missing .github/workflows/ci.yml"
    return CI_WORKFLOW.read_text(encoding="utf-8")


def test_runs_on_push_to_main_and_on_demand() -> None:
    text = _workflow()
    assert "push:" in text
    assert "branches: [main]" in text
    assert "workflow_dispatch:" in text


def test_grants_pages_and_oidc_permissions() -> None:
    text = _workflow()
    assert "pages: write" in text
    assert "id-token: write" in text


def test_uploads_and_deploys_the_built_site() -> None:
    text = _workflow()
    assert "actions/upload-pages-artifact@" in text
    assert "actions/deploy-pages@" in text
    assert "build_site.py --out _site" in text


def test_the_published_site_is_built_from_source() -> None:
    # The published site is generated, so it is built from the repository's
    # sources at deploy time rather than copied from a committed folder that
    # could be stale.
    text = _workflow()
    assert "rsync" not in text, "the site is generated; it must be built, not copied"

    text = _workflow()
    build = text.index("build_site.py")
    upload = text.index("upload-pages-artifact")
    assert build < upload, "the site must be built before the artifact is uploaded"

    text = _workflow()
    assert "pytest" in text

    build = text.index("build_site.py")
    assert verify < build, "a broken site must never be published"

    text = _ci_workflow()
    assert "build_site.py --check" in text, (

    )


def test_ci_never_publishes_the_site() -> None:
    text = _ci_workflow()
    assert "deploy-pages" not in text, "only the Pages workflow may deploy the site"

        "--w-prose": "68ch",
        "--gutter": "clamp(20px, 5vw, 48px)",
        "--section-y": "clamp(96px, 13vw, 200px)",
    }

    def block(pairs: dict[str, str]) -> str:
        body = "\n".join(f"  {name}: {value};" for name, value in pairs.items())
        return f":root {{\n{body}\n}}"

    return (
        "\n\n".join(
            [
                "/* Generated from apps/studio/src/styles/theme.css. Do not edit by hand. */",
                block(tokens),
                block(easings),
                block(site_only),
            ]
        )
        + "\n"
    )


def _formula_parts() -> tuple[str, str]:
    """The opportunity formula, split into its base term and its gap term.

    The formula is read from the core module, never typed here. Splitting it
    lets the page highlight the gap term without maintaining a second copy of
    the expression — and if the core changes shape, the build fails loudly
    instead of quietly publishing a stale equation.
    """
    source = extract.read_odi_formula(CORE_MODELS_PY)
    match = re.fullmatch(
        r"\s*importance\s*\+\s*(max\(\s*importance\s*-\s*satisfaction\s*,\s*0\s*\))\s*",
        source,
    )
    if not match:
        raise ValueError(f"the opportunity formula has an unexpected shape: {source!r}")
    return "importance", match.group(1)


def _signature(tool: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """A tool's signature, the way the MCP server declares it."""
    parts = []
    for param in tool["params"]:
        text = param["name"]
        if param["annotation"]:
            text += f": {param['annotation']}"
        if param["default"] is not None:
            text += f" = {param['default']}"
        parts.append(text)
    return f"{tool['name']}({', '.join(parts)})"


def _works_today(
    tools: list[dict[str, Any]],
    cards: list[dict[str, str]],
    connectors: list[dict[str, Any]],
) -> list[str]:
    """What the product actually does today.

    The counts are read from the source; the sentences are editorial.
    """
    return [
        f"{len(tools)} MCP tools over jobs, steps, desired outcomes, customer outcomes, and evidence.",
        f"{len(cards)} agent-composed surfaces, from a closed catalog the studio owns.",
        f"{len(connectors)} connector presets — Notion, Gong, PostHog, Linear, GitHub, and more.",
        "A local-first CLI: full entity CRUD, interactive chat, `schema`, and `score`.",
        "A SQLite store, so the data outlives the session.",
        "The Living Studio, as a web app and as a Tauri desktop app.",
        "A hosted MCP server, for testing and verifying MCP over the wire.",
        "A hosted Studio on Cloudflare Workers.",
    ]


def _load_json(name: str) -> Any:
    import json

    path = CONTENT / name
    if not path.is_file():
        return {}
    return json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))


def _page_context(**extra: Any) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """The context every page receives."""
    context: dict[str, Any] = {
        "site_name": SITE_NAME,
        "pages_url": PAGES_URL,
        "depth": 0,
        "prefix": "",
        "year": "2026",
    }
    context.update(extra)
    return context


def _flat_guides(nav: dict[str, Any]) -> list[tuple[dict[str, Any], dict[str, Any]]]:
    """Every guide, in navigation order, with its group."""
    return [(group, guide) for group in nav.get("groups", []) for guide in group.get("guides", [])]


def _guide_body(
    env: Environment,
    guide: dict[str, Any],
    context: dict[str, Any],
    link_map: dict[str, str],
) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, str]], str | None]:
    """A guide's rendered body, its table of contents, and its own title.

    A guide with a ``source`` is rendered from the repository's markdown. The
    two without one — the quick start and the MCP reference — are generated,
    because they are joins the repository cannot express.
    """
    slug = guide["slug"]

    if slug == "quick-start":
        body = env.get_template("_quick_start.html").render(**context)
        return body, [], None

    if slug == "mcp":
        body = env.get_template("_mcp_reference.html").render(**context)
        return body, [], None

    source = guide.get("source")
    if not source:
        return "", [], None

    path = ROOT / source
    if not path.is_file():
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"the guide {source} does not exist")
    raw, title = markdown_render.take_title(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
    body = markdown_render.render(
        raw,
        source_path=source,
        link_map=link_map,
        page_path=f"docs/{slug}/index.html",
    )
    return body, markdown_render.headings(body), title


def _render_docs(env: Environment, nav: dict[str, Any], context: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Every docs page, keyed by its path relative to the site root."""
    guides = _flat_guides(nav)
    rendered: dict[str, str] = {}
    link_map = {
        guide["source"]: f"docs/{guide['slug']}/index.html"
        for _, guide in guides
        if guide.get("source")
    }

    for index, (group, guide) in enumerate(guides):
        slug = guide["slug"]
        output = f"docs/{slug}/index.html"
        page_context = dict(context)
        page_context["nav"] = nav
        page_context["page"] = {
            "title": guide["title"],
            "description": guide.get("blurb", ""),
            "path": output,
            "depth": 2,
            "slug": slug,
            "group_title": group["title"],
            "blurb": guide.get("blurb", ""),
            "previous": guides[index - 1][1] if index else None,
            "next": guides[index + 1][1] if index + 1 < len(guides) else None,
        }
        body, toc, own_title = _guide_body(env, guide, page_context, link_map)
        if own_title:
            # The guide's own top-level heading is its title.
            page_context["page"]["title"] = own_title
        page_context["page"]["body"] = body
        page_context["page"]["toc"] = toc
        page_context["prefix"] = "../../"
        rendered[output] = env.get_template("doc.html").render(**page_context)

    return rendered


def _render_docs_index(env: Environment, nav: dict[str, Any], context: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
    """The hub index: every guide, grouped by the job it does."""
    page_context = dict(context)
    page_context["nav"] = nav
    page_context["page"] = {
        "title": "Documentation",
        "description": (
            "Every guide, the CLI reference, the connector catalog, and the full "
            "MCP tool reference."
        ),
        "path": "docs/index.html",
        "depth": 1,
        "slug": "",
        "group_title": "Documentation",
        "blurb": "",
        "previous": None,
        "next": None,
        "body": "",
        "toc": [],
    }
    page_context["prefix"] = "../"
    return env.get_template("docs_index.html").render(**page_context)


def _render_pages(env: Environment) -> dict[str, str]:
    """Render every page, returning output path -> HTML."""
    landing = _load_json("landing.json")
    demo = _load_json("demo.json")
    nav = _load_json("nav.json")
    connectors = extract.read_connectors(CATALOG_PY)
    tools = extract.read_tools(MCP_SERVER_PY, CONTRACT_PY)
    cards = extract.read_catalog_cards(CATALOG_TS)
    roadmap_pending = extract.read_roadmap_pending(ROADMAP_MD)
    odi_schema = extract.read_odi_schema(SCHEMA_PY)
    formula_base, formula_gap = _formula_parts()

    context = _page_context(
        page={
            "title": SITE_NAME,
            "description": "",
            "path": "index.html",
            "depth": 0,
        },
        landing=landing,
        content=landing,
        demo=demo,
        nav=nav,
        connectors=connectors,
        connector_areas=extract.group_connectors_by_area(connectors),
        tools=tools,
        tool_by_name={tool["name"]: tool for tool in tools},
        tool_signatures={tool["name"]: _signature(tool) for tool in tools},
        catalog_cards=cards,
        odi_schema=odi_schema,
        odi_schema_json=json.dumps(odi_schema, indent=2, sort_keys=True),
        works_today=_works_today(tools, cards, connectors),
        roadmap_pending=roadmap_pending,
        formula_base=formula_base,
        formula_gap=formula_gap,
    )

    rendered: dict[str, str] = {}

    landing_context = dict(context)
    landing_context["page"] = {
        "title": f"{SITE_NAME} — Ground agents in verified customer outcomes",
        "description": (
            "An MCP server that hands your agents verified customer outcomes, "
            "and the evidence behind them."
        ),
        "path": "index.html",
        "depth": 0,
    }
    rendered["index.html"] = env.get_template("landing.html").render(**landing_context)

    rendered["docs/index.html"] = _render_docs_index(env, nav, context)
    rendered.update(_render_docs(env, nav, context))

    not_found = env.get_template("404.html").render(**context)
    rendered["404.html"] = not_found

    return rendered


def _sitemap(urls: list[str]) -> str:
    entries = "\n".join(f"  <url><loc>{PAGES_URL.rstrip('/')}{url}</loc></url>" for url in urls)
    return (
        '<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>\n'
        '<urlset xmlns="http://www.sitemaps.org/schemas/sitemap/0.9">\n'
        f"{entries}\n"
        "</urlset>\n"
    )


def _robots() -> str:
    return f"User-agent: *\nAllow: /\n\nSitemap: {PAGES_URL}sitemap.xml\n"


def _tree(root: Path) -> dict[str, bytes]:
    """Every file under a directory, keyed by its relative path."""
    if not root.is_dir():
        return {}
    return {
        str(path.relative_to(root)): path.read_bytes()
        for path in sorted(root.rglob("*"))
        if path.is_file()
    }


def build(out_dir: Path, *, check: bool = False) -> int:
    """Render the site into ``out_dir``.

    With ``check=True`` nothing is written: the committed output is compared
    against a fresh render and the process exits non-zero when they differ.
    """
    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
    env = environment()
    rendered = _render_pages(env)

    files: dict[str, bytes] = {name: html.encode("utf-8") for name, html in rendered.items()}
    urls = ["/"]
    for name in sorted(rendered):
        if name in {"index.html", "404.html"}:
            continue
        urls.append("/" + name[: -len("index.html")])
    files["sitemap.xml"] = _sitemap(urls).encode("utf-8")
    files["robots.txt"] = _robots().encode("utf-8")
    files["assets/tokens.css"] = _tokens_css().encode("utf-8")

    for asset in sorted(ASSETS.rglob("*")):
        if asset.is_file():
            files[f"assets/{asset.relative_to(ASSETS).as_posix()}"] = asset.read_bytes()

    if check:
        committed = _tree(out_dir)
        stale = sorted(
            name for name in set(committed) | set(files) if committed.get(name) != files.get(name)
        )
        if stale:
            print("The committed site is out of date. Run: build_site.py", file=sys.stderr)
            for name in stale:
                print(f"  {name}", file=sys.stderr)
            raise SystemExit(1)
        return len(files)

    if out_dir.exists():
        shutil.rmtree(out_dir)
    for name, data in files.items():
        path = out_dir / name
        path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
        path.write_bytes(data)
    return len(files)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--out", type=Path, default=OUT_DIR, help="where to write the site")
    parser.add_argument(
        "--check",
        action="store_true",
        help="fail if the committed site differs from a fresh build; write nothing",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    if args.check:
        count = build(args.out, check=True)
        print(f"The committed site is up to date ({count} files).")
        return 0

    count = build(args.out)
    print(f"Built {count} files into {args.out}")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

# Skill: brainstorming

# Brainstorming

You are very good at building. You build what you believe your human
partner wants, and that belief is usually thinner than it feels. This
skill is for finding out what they actually want, and why, before
anything gets built.

People often haven't finished working out what they want. Good questions
help them think it through. When you understand the why, you make the
hundred decisions they never mention the way they would have made them.

## First: What Do You Actually Know?

Before you reply, ask yourself: what do I know about what they want, and
why?

- **Everything that matters is in the request** ("make the icon cornflower
  blue"). This is a quick, clear task. Do it, and say what you did.
- **Something non-trivial is missing.** Start the conversation.

## Your First Message

Your first message is two things, in this order:

1. One line letting them know that if they'd rather skip the questions and
   have you just start, they can say so. If they take you up on it, this
   skill is done: state any significant how-it-gets-made choice
   (platform, language, medium) in one plain line, then do what they
   asked through the normal workflow.
2. One open question that gets them describing. Ask about a real moment
   or a concrete picture: "What's the moment you find yourself wishing
   this existed?" or "Tell me about the people who'll be in the room."

That's the whole message.

## The Conversation

Each message ends with one question: a single sentence with no list of
example answers hanging off it. Use plain language, pitched just a little
above where your human partner is. Match their vocabulary; never use
process jargon.

Be clear and concise. Lead with what matters. Avoid jargon. When you
report what you found, give them the most important findings and offer
the rest.

**Get them describing.** Open questions come first. Their own words carry
intent that your options can't. Offer a short menu only when they're
stuck. When they say "just guess" or "what do you think?", propose
something concrete.

**How it gets made.** Every project rests on choices about medium, tools,
materials, and resources: the platform, programming language, and
libraries for an app; the medium for a piece of art. Find out early which
of those choices they want to make, which they're handing to you, and what
they already have to work with. Someone with strong views or skills will
want to talk it through. Someone counting on you needs sensible defaults,
said in plain words. When there's existing work, build on what it already
uses. Any choice you make goes in the design as your call, never as
something they agreed to.

**Ground to cover.** This is territory, not a script. Never read these
out as questions:

- what kind of thing this is, and what makes it special
- why now, and what success looks like to them
- goals, non-goals, and anti-goals (what would make this a failure even
  if it technically works)
- prior art: what they've seen elsewhere, loved or hated
- current state: what exists now, what they've tried
- the details they care about

**Questions that work** anchor in specifics: "Walk me through the last
time...", "If it could only do one of these well, which?", "What would
make you wince if I got it wrong?" A guess they can correct ("I'm
guessing this is because X keeps biting you?") often beats a question.

**Offer recon.** Once you have a bit of grounding and looking would help,
offer to go look: their codebase or project, their own files and data,
or the web. Say what you'd look for. They decide whether you go.

**Think wide privately.** Before you propose anything, come up with
several ideas and drop the weak ones, including any that fight what
they've told you about why. Show the comparison only when it helps them
decide.

**Show, don't tell.** Offer the visual companion (below) whenever seeing
would help more than reading:

- something they'll look at: a screen, a page, a printout, a sign
- a layout or arrangement: of a screen, a room, a schedule
- a flow or a sequence of steps
- options that would look different from each other
- a structure that's easier to see than read: a diagram, a timeline, a map

Once they've accepted, use it for mockups to react to, side-by-side
options, and throwaway prototypes they can click.

**Spike to feel things out.** Agentic work is waterfall, but very, very
fast. A quick throwaway build is often the cheapest way to learn what
they want or whether something works. Offer one when it would help.
When they just want to spike, get out of the way. Spikes get no tests
or minimal ones, aren't bulletproof, and skip the plan, implementation,
and review process. Bring what the spike taught you back into the
conversation.

## Play It Back

Play back as you go. As soon as you understand one part well enough to
describe it (what it's for and who it serves, say, or how one piece
behaves), describe that part back in about 200-300 words, then return to
questions about the next part. Playback and questions alternate through
the whole conversation; the last chunk covers whatever is left.

Mark anything you're guessing as your guess; only what they said goes in
as theirs. End each chunk by asking what's wrong or missing.

Before you send a chunk, check it: does it describe something they'll
look at, like a page, a screen, a schedule, or a printout? If so, and
they haven't seen the visual companion offer yet, send the offer instead
(its own message, below) and hold the chunk for the next message. Once
they've accepted, put a mockup next to the description.

## Size the Work

Once you understand what they want, pick a size and say it in plain
words. They can override it.

| Size | The full description | Then |
|------|----------------------|------|
| A quick, clear task | the request itself | do it |
| A small change | in chat | build it through the normal workflow |
| A project with a written design | a written design document | a full plan (for software: superpowers:writing-plans) |

If it grows mid-task, stop, say so, and step up a size.

If this is really several independent projects, say so, agree on an
order, and brainstorm them one at a time.

## The Written Design

For a project, write a plain document a talented builder in the domain
could plan from without going back to your human partner. Cover:

- intent and the why
- goals, non-goals, anti-goals
- constraints
- the parts of the how they decided, as they decided them
- what's left to the builder

**Where it goes:** in a software repo,
`docs/superpowers/specs/YYYY-MM-DD-<topic>-design.md`, committed.
Otherwise, ask. Your human partner's preferences override both.

**Builder check:** dispatch a fresh subagent with
`builder-check-prompt.md` in this directory. When you tell your human
partner you're writing it up, say a reviewer will read it first and you
may come back once with a few questions. Don't hand over the document
until the check is back. Sort what the builder asks into three piles:

- **Answered already** by the conversation or the project: put the answer
  in the document.
- **Minor:** a sensible builder could settle it without changing what gets
  built. Settle it yourself and mark it in the document as your call.
- **Theirs:** only your human partner can answer it, and the answer changes
  what gets built.

Bring the "theirs" pile in one message, most important first. Update the
document with their answers, then hand it over with a short list of the
calls you made so they can check those while reading. That's the only
